query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn system was selected to reduce cost while retaining the mechanical performance of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi; prior work reported comparable or better mechanical properties after excluding Co. Research on FeNiCrMn has mainly addressed corrosion, while studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys examined dynamic responses under tension or compression, different temperatures and strain rates, compositional changes, and the presence of cracks or voids. Those studies established that dynamic properties are sensitive to loading regime and material condition, but their different chemistries and defect states do not identify what governs FeNiCrMn. Under the constraints of retaining the Co-free composition and its strength–ductility balance, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains the dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes? Define a controlled study capable of testing the hypothesis, its applicable boundaries, the prior findings that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In as-solidified, Co‑free FeNiCrMn, the dynamic mechanical behavior across different temperatures and strain rates is governed by the interplay between rapid dislocation nucleation and localized adiabatic shear band (ASB) formation that triggers dynamic recrystallization. At high strain rates and/or low temperatures, the localized adiabatic heating and consequent ASB formation refine the microstructure, increasing yield strength but also promoting brittleness if uncontrolled.
generation.material_initial_state: As-solidified Co‑free FeNiCrMn with a primarily single-phase (likely FCC) structure and inherent solid solution microstructure.
generation.intervention: Perform dynamic mechanical tests (e.g., compression or tensile tests) at multiple controlled strain rates ranging from quasi‐static to high strain rates and over a range of temperatures (from cryogenic to elevated), followed by detailed post-deformation microstructural characterization (using SEM, TEM, and XRD) to identify the presence, morphology, and distribution of ASBs and recrystallized regions.
generation.conditions: Strain rate variation from quasi-static (~10^−3 s^−1) up to high dynamic rates (~10^3 s^−1) and temperatures spanning from cryogenic levels (≈77 K) to moderately elevated temperatures (e.g., ≈600 K).
generation.structural_mediator: Adiabatic shear bands that evolve under rapid plastic deformation, leading to localized dynamic recrystallization and microstructural refinement.
generation.mechanism: Under dynamic deformation, rapid dislocation nucleation combined with localized adiabatic heating causes the formation of shear bands. These shear bands act as sites for dynamic recrystallization that temporarily enhance local yield strength and work hardening. The balance between strain rate–induced strengthening (via dislocation motion and ASB formation) and the potential for embrittlement (from overly localized deformation) governs the observed strength–ductility performance.
generation.predicted_outcome: At higher strain rates and lower temperatures, we predict an increase in dynamic yield strength and pronounced ASB formation accompanied by microstructural refinement. Excessive localization (e.g., extensive ASB development) would correlate with reduced ductility, providing a measurable trade-off between strength and ductility. In contrast, at lower strain rates or moderate temperatures, a more uniform deformation pattern with improved ductility and less pronounced ASB features is expected.
generation.baseline: Quasi-static mechanical properties and microstructural features of as-solidified FeNiCrMn without significant ASB formation and dynamic recrystallization.
generation.boundary: This mechanistic hypothesis is expected to hold for as-solidified, single-phase Co‑free FeNiCrMn; variations in prior thermomechanical processing (e.g., annealing-induced phase changes) or significant changes in grain size/defect densities may lead to alternate deformation mechanisms.
generation.uncertainty: While the proposed mechanism is supported by analogous findings in related HEA systems, the exact thresholds for strain rate and temperature that trigger significant ASB formation and recrystallization in FeNiCrMn remain to be quantified. Additionally, contributions from other mechanisms (e.g., twinning or grain boundary sliding) may also play a role and need to be clearly distinguished.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare multiple as-solidified Co‑free FeNiCrMn samples. Subject samples to controlled compression tests over a matrix of strain rates (from ~10^−3 s^−1 to ~10^3 s^−1) and temperatures (77 K to 600 K). Follow each test with microstructural analysis (using SEM/TEM/XRD) to assess the presence and extent of ASBs and dynamic recrystallization. Compare mechanical property data (dynamic yield strength, strain hardening, ductility) with observed microstructural modifications.
measurements: Dynamic yield strength and stress–strain curves at each strain rate and temperature
Quantitative analysis of ASB density and width (using SEM/TEM)
Grain size and recrystallized volume fraction (using XRD and microscopy)
Fracture surface analysis to assess ductility vs. brittleness
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis would be falsified if no systematic correlation is observed between increased strain rate (or extreme temperature conditions) and the formation/intensity of adiabatic shear bands and related dynamic recrystallization. In particular, if samples at high strain rates do not show the predicted microstructural refinement (or if alternative deformation mechanisms dominate) despite corresponding changes in macroscopic strength and ductility, then the proposed mechanism would be refuted.

The work-hardening behavior of the HEAs was systematically analyzed by adopting the modified Ludwik model. The Cr element improved the local deformation characteristics, and the coordinated deformation of the dual phase was carried out, improving the nonuniform strain and promoting the strength and ductility balance of the alloys.

This study focuses on the cobalt-free medium-to-high-entropy alloys AlxCrFe2Ni2 and AlxTixCrFe2Ni2, investigating the influence of Alx and Tix (where x = 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, and 0.6) on the development of microstructural and mechanical properties in as-cast and annealed states. Structural changes were examined using optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurements, while mechanical properties were evaluated through Vickers hardness testing and compression testing. X-ray diffraction analysis of the AlxCrFe2Ni2 alloys confirmed that increasing the Al content in the as-cast state leads to the formation of a BCC phase, which completely dissolves into the FCC matrix after homogenization annealing. These single-phase alloys exhibit good ductility with relatively high strain hardening, such as the Al0.6CrFe2Ni2 alloy, which achieved a maximum compressive strength of σmax=1511 MPa at 50% deformation. A significant strengthening effect of Ti was observed in the AlxTixCrFe2Ni2 alloys, the mechanical properties of which are closely linked to the higher BCC phase content in the homogenized structure. reading.lever: Combine dynamic mechanical testing at varied strain rates with detailed post-deformation microstructure analysis on Co‑free FeNiCrMn.
reading.why: This approach, proven to capture strain rate sensitivity and deformation mechanisms in related HEAs, directly addresses the dynamic behavior gap in Co‑free FeNiCrMn.
